experiment_plans.feasibility_notes: The hypothesis is feasible given the compute and data assumptions. The AG News dataset is available with 120,000 training samples and 7,600 test samples, allowing for both fivefold cross-validation on the training set and evaluation on the held-out test set. The experiment can be conducted within a few hours on a single GPU node, using standard text classification models like BERT or RoBERTa variants.
experiment_plans.objective: To determine whether model performance rankings derived from fivefold cross-validation on the AG News training set differ significantly from those based on the held-out test set, as measured by Spearman rank correlation below 0.7.

independent: model performance metric (accuracy, F1-score) from 5-fold CV
model performance metric (accuracy, F1-score) from test set

experiment_plans.design: Comparative benchmarking of model performance rankings using two distinct evaluation methodologies: fivefold cross-validation on the training set and a single held-out test set evaluation. The experiment ranks models based on each method and computes the Spearman rank correlation between these rankings.

data_requirements.description: The AG News dataset contains 120,000 short news headlines and descriptions labeled into four categories (World, Sports, Business, Sci/Tech). This dataset is ideal for text classification tasks and provides sufficient size for robust cross-validation while maintaining a distinct test set for comparison.
preprocessing_steps: Load the CSV file using pandas.read_csv()
Map integer labels 0..3 to category names ('World', 'Sports', 'Business', 'Sci/Tech')
Split the training data into 5 folds for cross-validation
Use the provided test set (ag_news_document_text_category_classification_test.csv) for final evaluation

methods.name: Fivefold cross-validation
methods.description: Divides the training data into 5 equal parts, trains models on 4 parts and validates on the remaining part, repeating this process 5 times. Computes average performance metrics across all folds to estimate model stability and performance.

methods.name: Train-test split
methods.description: Uses the predefined train/test split of the AG News dataset to evaluate model performance on a held-out test set, providing an independent estimate of generalization capability.

evaluation.baseline: A Spearman correlation of 1.0 would indicate perfect agreement between CV and test set rankings, while a value of 0.7 or higher would suggest minimal disagreement.
evaluation.success_criteria: If the Spearman rank correlation between model rankings from 5-fold CV and the held-out test set is below 0.7, the hypothesis is supported. A correlation of 0.7 or higher would refute the hypothesis.

implementation_steps.description: Load the training data from ag_news_document_text_category_classification_train.csv and preprocess the text column by normalizing whitespace. Map integer labels to category names.
Initialize a list of candidate models (e.g., BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT) for text classification, ensuring they are compatible with the HPC environment and can run on a single GPU.
Perform fivefold cross-validation on the training data using scikit-learn's StratifiedKFold to maintain class distribution. For each fold, train each model and record its accuracy and F1-score.
Compute mean performance metrics (accuracy and F1-score) for each model across all 5 folds to establish CV rankings.
Evaluate each model on the held-out test set (ag_news_document_text_category_classification_test.csv) and record its accuracy and F1-score.
Rank models based on their average CV performance and their test set performance separately.
Calculate the Spearman rank correlation coefficient between the two sets of rankings using scipy.stats.spearmanr.
Output the correlation coefficient and determine whether it supports or refutes the hypothesis based on the threshold of 0.7.

risks: Insufficient model diversity to observe meaningful differences in rankings
Potential overfitting during cross-validation leading to inflated CV scores
Computational overhead from running multiple models on the same dataset
